transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m here because I keep feeling like I don’t deserve the trust people put in me. Small imperfections at work replay in my head, and I start thinking they mean I’m a dangerous doctor.

When these thoughts about being a 'dangerous doctor' come up, do they feel like unwanted, intrusive thoughts that pop into your mind against your will, or do they feel like an accurate reflection of how you generally see yourself?
They feel accurate to me. I replay little things I could have done better, and it feels like they show I don’t deserve people’s trust—that I’m a dangerous doctor.

Has this pattern of harshly judging yourself and feeling undeserving of trust been something you've experienced most of your life, or did it start more recently, perhaps alongside changes in your mood, sleep, or energy?
It started about a year and a month ago, after I received the clinic award.
Since this started about a year ago, has this low, self-critical feeling been present continuously, or has it come and gone with periods where you felt back to your normal self in between?
It’s been going on continuously since then—about a year and a month now, since I got that clinic award.

Before this current episode started about a year ago, had you ever experienced a similar period of low mood, self-critical thinking, or loss of interest that lasted two weeks or more at some point earlier in your life?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another period like this before the past year.
Over this past year, have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy level, or ability to concentrate that have been significant enough to affect your daily functioning?

My concentration has definitely been affected. I’ll read the same lab result or inbox message five times and still not feel sure what I just read. Even simple administrative decisions take me an embarrassing amount of time.
Over this past year, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even outside of work?

Yeah. I used to plan weekend hikes, go out for sunrise photos, cook big Indonesian dinners for friends. For the past few months, though, they just feel like obligations. I can’t really make myself care about doing them.
Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a major change in my sleep, honestly.
Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight, either an increase or a decrease?
No, I haven’t really noticed any significant change in my appetite or weight.
Over this past year, have you had any thoughts of death, of not wanting to be alive, or of harming yourself?
I don’t have a plan to kill myself. But sometimes, especially after a day when I feel like I’ve let patients down, I think it might be better if I just didn’t wake up.

Before the past year, did you ever go through a longer stretch—two years or more—where you generally felt down, self-critical, or joyless most of the time, even if it wasn't as intense as what you're feeling now?
I don’t think so. I can’t really point to a period that long where I felt that way most of the time.
